# Architecture decision records

**Status.** Index — regenerated by hand when an ADR is added or its Status changes.

An ADR records **why** a decision was made, at the moment it was made, and what
would reverse it. It is **frozen** once accepted: the only line that ever changes
afterwards is `Status`. A correction is a new ADR, never an annotation on an old
one — [ADR-010](ADR-010-one-roadmap-one-rule.md) §8.1 rule 3.

Three consequences worth knowing before you read one:

- **An ADR is not status.** What is done, in flight and next is
  [ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md), and nowhere else.
- **An ADR's paths describe the tree as it was.** ADR-001 cites
  `Editor/src/Exported/Characters/`, which is where the characters lived in
  August 2026 and is not where they live now. `scripts/check_docs.py`
  deliberately does not check paths inside this directory, for exactly that
  reason.
- **An ADR's line citations into `ARCHITECTURE.md` resolve against the frozen
  copy**, [`docs/archive/ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-12.md`](../archive/README.md) —
  approximately, and that README says by how much. Everything written from here
  on cites by anchor.

## Writing one

A work package that grows a decision gets an ADR, `Proposed`, **with a
recommended default** — so the plan still runs if nobody answers. If the default
is safe and reversible, proceed under it and say so in
[ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md); if it is not, stop, leave the ADR, and end with the
tree green.

Number it next, name the file `ADR-NNN-<slug>.md`, open with a `Status` line in
the first ten lines (`scripts/check_docs.py` checks that much), and add a row
above. State what would **reverse** the decision: a decision with no reversal
condition is a preference.
